notes: Corrected the placement of 'of': the Hebrew writes glory as the bare direct object and 'from upon me' as the ablative; the ASV's 'stripped me of my glory' inverts the two, so 'of' is the verb's supplied preposition to its own object (rule 44) and מֵעַל is left with no word for its relation (rule 40). Compare JOB.19.13, where the same מֵעָלַי is rendered directly as 'from me' and keeps the word.
